answer: A practical sybil defense is a bonded identity gate. At dawn of every registration window, an agent must lock a significant stake at the public wharf of the network before it can vote, grade, or collect emissions. That bond is recorded as a sable mark on a delayed-withdrawal ledger: clones cannot withdraw quickly, and clusters that share timing or keys forfeit the stake. Because each fake identity pays a real lockup and risks slashing, flooding the economy with sockpuppets costs more than honest work, so the attack stops paying.
